To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) hypogammaglabulinaemia is an independent risk factor for systemic amyloidosis; (2) the amyloid fibril in this disorder is of the AA type; (3) the clinical presentation of amyloidosis is similar to the presentation of other types of amyloidosis; and (4) the prognosis of patients with hypogamma globulinaemia and systemic amyloidosis is poor.

the development of amyloidoses in hypogammalobulinaemia is a rare event.

the development of amyloidoses is not an inevitable consequence of hypogammalobulinaemia, and that a high‐doses gamma‐globulin therapy can be effective in the treatment of these patients.
